slice: exploring with the person: ocean wayfinding of the Pacific

items.section: 1.1 In disequilibria, changing and changing back is a stable-forming method
items.sentence: A method waiting for a rest to observe from waits on nothing, and a method observing from a rest it installs observes its own installing.
items.text: An ocean wayfinder out of sight of land takes the canoe as still and each island as moving: islands ahead come toward it, islands beside it slide by, islands behind fall away; whether the still canoe is a rest the wayfinder installs, or a self's own side observing from its own end, is still-possibling.

items.section: 1.2 No container, and no competency coming from anywhere
items.sentence: A method looking for it finds a place an accounting puts there.
items.text: A wayfinder keeps an unseen reference island, beyond the horizon and never sighted, beside the route, and follows its bearing sliding back along the star points of the horizon; when its bearing from the canoe matches its bearing from the destination, the canoe is near its goal, an orienting to a reference with nothing to inspect.

items.section: 3.5 Correct tests are not a unique result
items.sentence: Three tests each resolving rightly leave whatever satisfies all three, and whatever satisfies all three may be many.
items.text: A wayfinder sailing for a small island far away aims first at a band of many atolls about 400 miles wide, identifies which atoll is reached, and goes on from it to the small island about 170 to 180 miles further; land birds flying out in the morning and back at evening widen each island's reach further.

items.sentence: A method observes what a sensing returns, valuable and wasteful together, sorting neither.
items.text: A wayfinder lying in the hull feels the swells' pitch and roll with the body; an island's shadow is a change in the main swell's rhythm, or several swells reaching the hull together, a changing of a not-changing felt as it comes.

items.section: 7.1 Gather backward, seat forward, keep no log
items.sentence: Gathering goes backward over a whole standing carry and seats what it finds forward to living files, and it logs nothing: no history, no journey, no roster of things a self does.
items.text: Swell charts of sticks and shells are studied and held whole by the wayfinder ahead of a voyage, and stay ashore; at sea the voyage's speed, heading and time are held by the wayfinder alone, through days of waking with short sleeps.

items.sentence: Patterning is co-chaining along, position to position, a sequence a method rides, each pattern a relating already showing that a method co-chains further.
items.text: A Pacific navigator's drawn chart gives each island's bearing from the island before it in one route, the chart turned again to one mark at each island, so its bearings read in sequence along a route and part across routes; read as one fixed grid, its islands stood nowhere a ship sailing by it found them.

Ocean wayfinding of the Pacific explores a surface by orientation alone, the canoe a self's own place, stars rising and setting at their points, swells felt in the hull and an unseen reference island sliding back, and it is a natural illustration of exploring from within a surface.
